items.passage:
Wenhua holds the strap of the night bus
as Shanghai slides past in wet neon,
her son Jianguo beside her with one suitcase
and a ticket north folded in his shirt.
For eighteen years her rule was plain:
home before the last bus, no matter what.
Tonight she counts the stops and wonders
whether a rule can travel a thousand miles.
She does not repeat it. She does not cancel it.
She only lets it hang between them, ______,
like a lantern no one lights or takes down,
while Jianguo watches her reflection in the glass
and understands that she is waiting for him
to decide what it should mean from now on.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: forbidden
unresolved
forgotten
enforced
items.explanation: Wenhua는 규칙을 다시 말하지도, 취소하지도 않는다고 묘사된다. 또한 아무도 켜거나 내리지 않는 등불에 비유되며, 아들이 그 의미를 정하기를 기다린다고 한다. 따라서 규칙이 결론 나지 않은 채 남아 있다는 뜻의 B가 가장 적절하다. A와 D는 규칙을 금지하거나 강제한다는 뜻이라 '취소하지도 반복하지도 않는다'는 단서와 맞지 않고, C는 그녀가 규칙을 계속 의식하는 장면과 모순된다.

items.passage: Three rules governed the reading room in Krakow where I taught that first winter: whisper, return what you borrow, and never ask Marta why. Marta was fifteen and kept a library atlas in her bag for two months past its due date. I am Consuelo, and I was new enough to believe a polite reminder would settle things. It did not. Each time I mentioned the atlas, Marta grew quieter, folding her arms as if guarding something. Eventually the head librarian told me the atlas had belonged to a teacher Marta's grandfather once studied under. I stopped reminding her. My silence was not indifference but a kind of ______: I would wait for her to bring the book back when the waiting was hers to end. In April, she slid it across my desk without a word, a pressed leaf marking a page of mountain ranges.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: surrender
suspicion
patience
neglect
items.explanation: Consuelo는 아틀라스의 사연을 알고 나서 독촉을 멈추고, Marta가 스스로 끝낼 때까지 기다리겠다고 말한다. 또한 그 침묵이 무관심(indifference)이 아니라고 분명히 밝힌다. 따라서 기다림을 뜻하는 C가 가장 적절하다. A는 포기를 뜻해 의도적 기다림과 맞지 않고, B는 사연을 이해한 뒤의 태도와 반대되며, D는 무관심과 같은 뜻이라 지문이 직접 부정한다.

items.passage: Vermont winters kept Katerina's stall busy, though she had trained as a seamstress and only took up boots when the mill closed. Albert, her one apprentice, arrived at sixteen convinced that repair was a lesser trade. His teacher had once told him that anyone who fixed things lacked the imagination to make them. For weeks he stitched heels with visible reluctance. Then Katerina handed him a pair of work boots resoled four times, each repair in a different thread, and asked him to read them. He traced the seams and saw a farmer's whole decade: the year of the flood, the year of the new tractor. After that, his view of the work was ______. He no longer called it patching; he called it keeping a record, and he signed his stitches with a small knot only Katerina could find.
items.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: confirmed
concealed
diminished
transformed
items.explanation: 처음 Albert는 수선을 하찮은 일로 여겼지만, 장화의 바느질 자국에서 한 농부의 10년을 읽어낸 뒤 그것을 '기록을 남기는 일'이라고 부르게 된다. 이처럼 생각이 완전히 바뀌었으므로 D가 가장 적절하다. A는 원래 생각이 굳어졌다는 뜻이라 변화와 반대이고, B는 그가 생각을 숨겼다는 근거가 없다. C는 수선을 더 낮게 보게 됐다는 뜻이라 존중이 커진 결말과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: On the first Monday of November, the movie theater in Vienna was closed for the season, and Bao had rented its empty stage for lessons. Linus arrived with his violin and a list of complaints. The hall was cold, the seats smelled of dust, and nothing about this city resembled the conservatory he had left. Bao listened, tuned his A string sharply, and said they would begin with open strings, as beginners do. Linus played them with exaggerated boredom. Then the note rose into the dark balcony and returned to him, rounder and slower than any sound he had made at home. He stopped. He played it again, softly this time, and waited for the echo as if it might answer a question. Bao said nothing, but she moved her chair closer, and for the rest of the hour neither of them looked at the clock.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From grudging resentment toward the lesson to quiet absorption in the hall's sound
From open admiration for Bao to disappointment in her old-fashioned methods
From nervous excitement about the city to calm indifference toward the music
From playful teasing between the two to tense rivalry over the instrument
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Linus는 불평 목록을 들고 오고 지루한 척 개방현을 켜며 불만을 드러낸다. 그러나 소리가 발코니에서 메아리쳐 돌아오자 그는 멈추고, 부드럽게 다시 연주하며 그 소리에 몰입한다. 따라서 불만에서 몰입으로의 전환을 말한 A가 정답이다. B는 처음에 Bao를 존경했다는 근거가 없고, C와 D는 각각 무관심과 경쟁이라는 결말이 지문의 몰입한 분위기와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: We had rented the farmhouse outside Chengdu for the spring, and Lanying had come only to measure its boundaries for the new road. Jiayi, who had kept the house for its absent owners for nine years, showed her each room with crisp efficiency: here the drainage, here the cracked beam, here the line where the old wall once stood. Lanying took notes and asked few questions. In the last room, a straw hat hung from a nail beside the window, its brim softened by years of sun. Lanying reached to move it out of her way. Jiayi caught her wrist, then let go as if surprised by her own hand. "That was the grandmother's," she said, more quietly than she had said anything all morning. "She wore it to check the rice. Nobody has taken it down." Lanying lowered her tape measure and did not lift it again.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From suspicious hostility toward the surveyor to warm and open friendliness
From brisk, practical description of the house to hushed, personal reverence
From nostalgic sorrow for the owners to brisk impatience with the survey
From humorous exaggeration about the farmhouse to sober technical precision
items.explanation: 처음에 Jiayi는 배수, 갈라진 들보 등을 '간결하고 효율적으로' 설명한다. 그러나 할머니의 밀짚모자 앞에서 그녀는 아침 내내 중 가장 조용한 목소리로 말하고, Lanying도 줄자를 내린다. 따라서 실용적인 설명에서 경건하고 개인적인 분위기로 바뀐다는 B가 정답이다. A는 처음의 적대감 근거가 없고, C와 D는 전환의 방향이 반대이거나 유머라는 근거가 없다.

items.passage:
By dusk the storm had moved east of the Delta,
and Mattie stood at the soccer field's edge, baton in her coat pocket,
counting the puddles as if they were missed rehearsals.
Ivy, the youngest of her violinists, ran ahead in rain boots,
laughing at the mud that swallowed her steps.
Mattie called her back, sharp as a downbeat.
Then Ivy knelt where the goal post leaned
and lifted something the water had uncovered:
a tin box, rusted, a child's name scratched on its lid.
Inside, a folded program from a concert forty years gone,
and Mattie's own name printed small at the bottom.
She took it without a word. The field went still.
She held the paper the way one holds a bird,
and Ivy, who had never seen her conductor hesitate,
waited beside her without asking anything at all.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From grief over the storm's damage to relief that the field survived
From quiet nostalgia for the past to irritation at Ivy's behavior
From brisk, mildly impatient supervision to hushed, tender astonishment
From cheerful celebration of the concert to anxious fear of the weather
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Mattie는 웅덩이를 놓친 리허설처럼 세고 Ivy를 날카롭게 불러들이는 등 엄격한 지휘자의 모습이다. 그러나 40년 전 자신의 이름이 적힌 공연 프로그램이 나오자 들판은 고요해지고, 그녀는 종이를 새처럼 조심스럽게 든다. 따라서 조급한 감독에서 조용한 경이로의 전환을 말한 C가 정답이다. A는 폭풍 피해에 대한 슬픔이 없고, B와 D는 전환 방향이 지문과 반대다.

items.passage: Four flights of stairs, two locked doors, and one rusted ladder separated our apartment from the water tank on the roof in Naples, and my father, Marco, climbed them every Sunday to check the float valve. I, Giada, followed him for years without speaking much; his Italian and my English had grown apart until our conversations shrank to instructions. Hand me the wrench. Hold the light. I used to treat these climbs as a chore and a joke, counting the steps aloud to annoy him. One Sunday the valve stuck, and while he worked he began, unprompted, to describe the village tank he had climbed as a boy, the one his own father had built. He spoke slowly, mixing both languages, searching my face to see if I followed. I did. I sat on the tank's edge with the light steady in my hand, and the city below seemed to lower its voice so I could hear him.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From fond admiration for the father to frustration at his stubborn silence
From anxious worry about the broken valve to relief once it is repaired
From formal respect for family tradition to casual indifference toward it
From detached, slightly mocking routine to attentive, intimate listening
items.explanation: Giada는 처음에 지붕 오르기를 귀찮은 일이자 농담으로 여기고 계단 수를 세며 아버지를 놀렸다고 말한다. 그러나 아버지가 어린 시절 마을 물탱크 이야기를 꺼내자 그녀는 불빛을 든 채 집중해 듣고 도시마저 조용해진 듯 느낀다. 따라서 무심하고 조롱 섞인 일상에서 친밀한 경청으로의 전환을 말한 D가 정답이다. A, B, C는 각각 감정의 방향이 반대이거나 밸브 수리 결과처럼 지문의 초점이 아닌 내용을 다룬다.

items.passage: Years later, I can still smell the burnt coffee of that train-station cafe in Tromso, where my brother Thorvald and I waited for the call about his discharge papers. He had come home on leave, but whether he would have to return north depended on a decision being made somewhere far away. For the first hour I chattered at him, inventing games with sugar packets, reading the departure board aloud in silly voices, sure that if I kept him laughing the phone would ring with good news. He played along. Then I noticed his hand on the table. It was resting perfectly still, palm down, the way he must have learned to hold it somewhere I had never been. I stopped talking. I put my own hand beside his, not touching, and we watched the snow fill the empty tracks until the waitress came to say there was a call for him.
items.question: Which choice best describes the shift in tone that occurs in the text?
options: From restless, playful distraction to subdued, watchful solemnity
From bitter resentment toward the army to forgiving acceptance of it
From calm confidence about the news to frantic panic before the call
From quiet sadness about the war to cheerful relief at his homecoming
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 설탕 봉지 게임과 우스운 목소리로 오빠를 웃기려 애쓰며 들뜬 모습을 보인다. 그러나 오빠의 손이 낯선 방식으로 완전히 멈춰 있는 것을 보고 말을 멈추며, 조용히 눈을 지켜본다. 따라서 장난스러운 주의 돌리기에서 숙연한 침묵으로의 전환을 말한 A가 정답이다. B의 군대에 대한 원망, C의 공황, D의 기쁜 안도는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Words were Malek's first gift to every keeper he trained. At the lighthouse station on the edge of Cairo's old harbor district, he now taught them to his granddaughter, Dalia, who had grown up speaking only the language of her mother's country. Each evening he named a part of the lamp in Arabic, and she repeated it, stumbling, while the beam swept the dark water. She told him she was learning only to please him, that she would leave for her studies abroad in the fall and forget it all. He did not argue. One night the power failed, and Malek, his eyes weak, asked her to talk him through the backup switches. She found herself calling each one by the name he had taught her, without translating. When the light returned, she did not mention her plans, and the next evening she arrived before he did, notebook already open.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes a power failure, then flashes back to explain why the lighthouse matters to Malek.
It presents a routine and a character's dismissive stance, then shows an event that quietly alters it.
It contrasts two characters' memories of the lighthouse, then reveals which memory is accurate.
It lists the parts of the lamp, then explains how each part was named by an earlier keeper.
items.explanation: 지문은 먼저 할아버지가 매일 저녁 램프 부품의 아랍어 이름을 가르치는 일상과, Dalia가 곧 떠나 잊을 것이라는 무심한 태도를 제시한다. 이후 정전이라는 사건에서 그녀는 번역 없이 그 이름을 쓰게 되고, 다음 날 먼저 와서 공책을 펼친다. 따라서 일상과 태도 제시 후 그것을 조용히 바꾸는 사건을 보여준다는 B가 정답이다. A는 회상 구조가 없고, C와 D는 기억 대조나 부품 이름의 유래 설명이 지문에 없다.

items.passage: Who decides what a courtyard is for? Narong had asked this, loudly, the morning he found the fountain in their Hanoi courtyard drained and a stack of tiles beside it. Thida, his stepmother, had arranged for it to be rebuilt as a planting bed without consulting anyone. The fountain had stopped working years before, but his mother used to sit on its rim in the evenings, and Narong had kept sitting there after she died. For three days he refused to speak to Thida, eating at odd hours and slamming the gate. On the fourth day he found her kneeling in the empty basin, laying the old fountain's chipped blue tiles into the border of the new bed, one by one, in the pattern they had always made. She did not look up. He watched for a long time, then crouched and handed her the next tile.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It recounts a conflict from Thida's point of view, then shifts to Narong's memories of his mother.
It describes the history of the fountain, then explains how the courtyard was designed originally.
It opens with a challenge to a decision, explains the hurt behind it, and ends with a gesture of reconciliation.
It presents an argument between two characters, then reveals that the argument was a misunderstanding.
items.explanation: 지문은 '누가 마당의 용도를 정하는가'라는 Narong의 항의로 시작해, 분수가 어머니와의 추억이 담긴 장소였다는 상처의 이유를 설명한다. 마지막에는 Thida가 옛 타일을 새 화단에 놓고 Narong이 다음 타일을 건네는 화해의 몸짓으로 끝난다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 Thida의 시점이 아니고, B는 마당의 원래 설계 설명이 없으며, D는 갈등이 오해였다는 내용이 없다.

items.passage: "Your dryer's still running," Mika said, not looking up from her magazine. I had not expected to see her at the Auckland laundromat, and certainly not on the bench beside mine. Mika and I share a wall, and for six weeks we had shared a silence, ever since I complained about her music in a note I regretted the moment I slid it under her door. I, Tui, had written an apology twice and torn it up both times. Now, folding towels, I rehearsed it again in my head and found every version stiff and lawyerly. Then her basket tipped, and a dozen socks rolled under the machines. Without discussing it, we both got down on the linoleum to collect them. By the time we stood up, laughing at a sock that was clearly neither of ours, the apology no longer seemed like a speech I owed her. It seemed like something I could simply say, and I did.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes a quarrel in detail, then argues that apologies are usually unnecessary between neighbors.
It explains why the narrator moved, then compares two laundromats the narrator has visited.
It presents Mika's view of the conflict, then contrasts it with the narrator's later explanation.
It opens in a chance meeting, recalls an unresolved conflict, and then shows a small accident easing it.
items.explanation: 지문은 빨래방에서의 우연한 대화 한 줄로 시작해, 쪽지 사건 이후 6주간의 침묵과 찢어버린 사과문을 회상한다. 이어 양말 바구니가 엎어지는 작은 사고로 함께 웃게 되면서 사과가 자연스러워진다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 사과가 불필요하다는 주장을 하지 않고, B의 이사·빨래방 비교는 없으며, C는 Mika의 관점이 제시되지 않는다.

items.passage: Twelve looms, two thermoses, and one radio that only found a single station: that was the night shift at the weaving cooperative in Kyoto when I joined it. Jomo had come from Nairobi on a craft fellowship that paid for his room but nothing else, and I, Takeshi, was finishing an apprenticeship that paid even less. Visitors from the day tours admired our sashes behind glass and asked if we were artists. We said yes, because the alternative was explaining that admiration did not cover rent. At two in the morning, Jomo and I traded small, practical kindnesses: a spare bobbin, a warmed rice ball, a hand to hold a warp taut. I once believed those nights were a waiting room before real work began. Looking back, I see they were the work, and that the pay we never received was partly made up in what we taught each other.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It sets out the conditions of a past job, then reinterprets their meaning from a later vantage point.
It praises the cooperative's sashes, then describes how visitors learned to weave them on tours.
It compares Jomo's homeland with Kyoto, then explains why he chose to remain in Japan.
It recounts a dispute over unpaid wages, then describes how the cooperative finally resolved it.
items.explanation: 지문은 베틀 열두 대, 보온병 두 개 같은 목록으로 야간 근무의 조건과 무급 노동 상황을 먼저 제시한다. 마지막 부분에서 화자는 '돌이켜보면' 그 밤들이 대기실이 아니라 진짜 일이었다고 의미를 재해석한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 관광객이 직조를 배운다는 내용이 없고, C의 고향 비교와 D의 임금 분쟁 해결은 지문에 나오지 않는다.

items.passage: A wooden spoon tapped twice against the pot was Mandla's signal that dinner was late, and Nandi heard it all the way up in the old projection booth. She had turned the booth above her aunt's cinema in Addis Ababa into a kitchen of her own, with a hot plate and a shelf of spices, and she cooked there whenever she wanted to be left alone. Tonight Mandla climbed the narrow stairs and announced that the stew needed more salt. Nandi answered that it was perfect. They argued about salt for ten minutes, voices rising over the hum of the cooling projector. __Neither of them mentioned the letter from the culinary school in Nairobi, still unopened on the shelf between the cumin and the cardamom.__ At last Mandla tasted the stew again, set down the spoon, and said quietly that perhaps it was fine after all.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains why Mandla dislikes the spices Nandi keeps in the booth.
It suggests that the argument about salt stands in for a larger, unspoken disagreement.
It reveals that Nandi has already decided to reject the culinary school's offer.
It shows that Mandla is unaware that Nandi has applied to any school.
items.explanation: 두 사람은 소금 문제로 10분이나 언성을 높이지만, 밑줄 문장은 둘 다 아직 뜯지 않은 요리학교 편지에 대해서는 말하지 않는다고 알려준다. 마지막에 Mandla가 조용히 물러서는 모습까지 함께 보면, 소금 다툼이 더 큰 갈등을 대신하고 있음을 알 수 있다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A는 향신료에 대한 반감 근거가 없고, C는 편지가 아직 열리지 않았으므로 맞지 않으며, D는 '둘 다' 언급하지 않는다는 표현과 모순된다.

items.passage: When the last student left the language school classroom in Tehran, Nasrin stayed behind to wipe the whiteboard, as she had every Thursday since she was eleven. Yitzhak, who had taught there with her father for twenty years, always stacked the chairs while she cleaned. Her father had moved abroad long ago and called rarely; Yitzhak had never once spoken of him. They worked in silence, she erasing verb tables, he lining the chairs into neat towers. Tonight, as she reached the board's top corner, she found a single word written small in her father's handwriting, faded but never erased: her name. __Yitzhak glanced at it, then went back to stacking the chairs, slower than before.__ She understood then that he had cleaned around it for years, and that the Thursday chore had never been only about the classroom.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It shows that Yitzhak resents Nasrin for discovering her father's handwriting.
It reveals that Yitzhak had never noticed the word on the board before tonight.
It hints, through a small change in Yitzhak's pace, that he knew of the word and its meaning.
It suggests that Yitzhak is eager to explain her father's departure in detail.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장에서 Yitzhak는 단어를 힐끗 보고 평소보다 느리게 의자를 쌓는다. 이어지는 문장에서 Nasrin은 그가 수년간 그 글씨를 지우지 않고 피해서 닦아 왔음을 깨닫는다. 따라서 그의 작은 동작 변화가 그가 이미 그 단어와 의미를 알고 있었음을 암시한다는 C가 정답이다. A의 원망, B의 처음 발견, D의 설명하려는 열망은 지문의 침묵과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Beirut's oldest ceramics studio sits above a tire shop, and that is where Samira and I, Kwesi, spent every Saturday after her family moved across the city. Distance made our friendship deliberate; we had to plan it now, and the studio became our fixed point. Last spring, one of my bowls was chosen for a gallery show downtown. Samira hugged me in the doorway and said she had always known. Then, over the following weeks, she began arriving late, leaving early, finding reasons to work at the far wheel. __One Saturday I found her old glaze test tiles, the ones we had made together our first month, boxed and labeled for the shelf marked "give away."__ I did not ask about them. Instead, I brought the box back to our table and set it between us, and after a while she took out a tile and began, very carefully, to describe what she had hoped it would become.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It explains how the narrator first learned to mix glazes at the studio.
It reveals that Samira has decided to stop making ceramics altogether.
It shows that the studio has begun discarding work by former members.
It offers concrete evidence of Samira's withdrawal that prompts the narrator to act.
items.explanation: 앞부분은 화자의 성공 이후 Samira가 늦게 오고 일찍 떠나는 등 점점 멀어지는 모습을 보여준다. 밑줄 문장은 두 사람이 함께 만든 타일이 '기증' 선반에 놓인 것을 발견하는 장면으로, 그 거리감을 구체적으로 보여준다. 이를 본 화자가 상자를 다시 테이블로 가져오므로 D가 정답이다. A는 유약 배합 학습과 무관하고, B는 그녀가 도자기를 그만둔다는 근거가 없으며, C는 스튜디오의 정책에 대한 내용이 없다.

items.passage: By the third week of proofs, the printing press room on the Cornish coast smelled of ink and sea salt, and Casey and I had stopped agreeing on anything. I, Jonah, had written a memoir about walking home from my grandmother's village as a boy; Casey was translating it, and she kept asking questions I could not answer. Which road had I taken? How far was the river from the chapel? I insisted the details did not matter. __Then she unrolled a hand-drawn map across the press bed, my route traced in pencil from my own sentences, with three gaps where my memory had simply skipped ahead.__ I stared at those blank stretches for a long while. That afternoon I phoned my aunt, who still lived in the village, and asked her to tell me the way home, step by step, as if I had never walked it.
items.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It marks a turning point by making the narrator confront the gaps in his own account.
It shows that Casey has decided to abandon the translation because of the errors.
It explains how the press room came to be used for printing local maps.
It reveals that the narrator had intentionally invented parts of the route.
items.explanation: 밑줄 문장 이전에 Jonah는 세부 사항이 중요하지 않다고 고집한다. 그러나 Casey가 그의 문장으로 그린 지도에서 기억이 비어 있는 세 구간을 보여주자, 그는 한참 바라본 뒤 숙모에게 전화해 길을 묻는다. 따라서 밑줄 문장은 화자가 자기 기록의 공백을 직면하게 하는 전환점이므로 A가 정답이다. B의 번역 포기, C의 인쇄소 역사, D의 의도적 날조는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: I watched my grandmother, Solange, shape the morning loaves at the Lisbon bakery an hour before the shutters opened, the way I had watched her since I was small enough to sit on the flour sacks. In three days I, Anselmo, would board a ship for a job across the ocean, and I had come to say a proper goodbye. I had prepared a speech. She handed me an apron instead. For an hour we worked side by side, and she corrected my folding with a flick of her knuckle, never once mentioning my departure. At first her silence stung; I wanted her to say she would miss me. But as the ovens warmed, I noticed she had set aside a small, tightly wrapped loaf, the kind that keeps for a week, and that she was teaching me, fold by fold, how to make it myself.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Solange by the end of the text?
options: He comes to appreciate that her lessons express care she does not state aloud.
He remains hurt that she refuses to acknowledge his decision to leave.
He feels amused by her strictness and doubts the value of her methods.
He grows impatient with her and wishes he had left without visiting.
items.explanation: Anselmo는 처음에 할머니가 떠남을 언급하지 않아 서운해한다. 그러나 오래 보관되는 빵을 따로 싸 두고 그 빵 만드는 법을 하나하나 가르쳐 주는 모습을 보며, 그것이 말하지 않은 애정 표현임을 깨닫는다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 처음의 감정에만 해당하고, C의 회의와 D의 조급함은 지문의 흐름과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Alonso had taught geography in the village for forty years, and he still spoke as if every bus leaving the Galician depot were a lesson. Fatma, once his brightest pupil, now drove the morning route, and she let him ride free in the front seat. Today her small son rode with them. Halfway to the coast, the boy asked Alonso why he never visited the cities he had taught about. Alonso began an answer about railways and expense, then about his late wife's health, then about the weather in Madrid. The boy listened with a frown. Fatma kept her eyes on the road. She remembered how certain Alonso had sounded in class, how he had made every distant place seem within reach, and she felt something gentler than disappointment watching him stumble now. When they reached the coast, she pulled over a moment longer than necessary, so he could see the water before getting off.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Alonso?
options: Openly mocking, highlighting his excuses to diminish his former authority
Sympathetic, noting his evasions while treating his vulnerability with kindness
Coldly neutral, reporting his words without suggesting any emotional response
Reverent, presenting him as wiser than the boy who questions him
items.explanation: 서술자는 Alonso가 철도, 아내의 건강, 날씨로 대답을 계속 돌리는 모습을 그대로 보여주어 그의 회피를 드러낸다. 동시에 Fatma가 실망보다 부드러운 감정을 느끼고, 그가 바다를 볼 수 있게 차를 잠시 더 세우는 장면을 통해 그의 약함을 따뜻하게 감싼다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 조롱, C의 냉정한 중립, D의 숭배는 회피와 연민이 함께 담긴 서술과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage:
Three kites hung drying in the Rotterdam yard,
two red, one patched with a map of somewhere else,
the day after we buried our uncle.
Emil spoke first, in the voice of lists:
the stairs, the stove, the doctor's warnings,
the home outside the city with a garden view.
Ingrid wound string around her fingers
and said our aunt still climbed to this yard every morning
to test the wind for kites no one would buy.
I said nothing, cousin to them both.
I watched our aunt through the kitchen window,
her hands smoothing paper as if the house were listening,
and I understood that both of them were right,
and that the yard, not the stairs,
was what we were really deciding to take from her.
items.question: Which choice best describes the speaker's attitude toward the decision about the aunt?
options: Firmly convinced that moving her is the only responsible choice
Dismissive of both cousins' concerns as exaggerated and selfish
Torn, recognizing the sense of each view and the loss either entails
Indifferent, since the speaker plans to leave the matter to the cousins
items.explanation: 화자는 실용적 이유를 나열하는 Emil과 숙모의 매일의 습관을 말하는 Ingrid 모두가 옳다고 깨닫는다. 또한 마지막에서 결국 계단이 아니라 마당을 그녀에게서 빼앗게 된다고 말하며 어느 쪽이든 상실이 따른다는 것을 인식한다. 따라서 양쪽을 이해하며 갈등하는 C가 정답이다. A는 한쪽만 지지하고, B는 두 사람이 옳다는 표현과 모순되며, D는 화자가 깊이 관찰하는 모습과 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Two coffee cups set out on the galley counter every morning: that was Dolores's habit for eleven years after her husband died. She had cooked for his crew on the old cargo ship moored in Havana harbor, and when the ship became a floating restaurant, she stayed on in its narrow galley. I, Daphne, delivered her produce each dawn. At first I found the second cup a little sad and a little strange, and I placed the onions carefully around it as if it were fragile. One morning she poured coffee into both cups and handed the second to me. "He would want it used," she said, and nothing more. I drank it standing up, too surprised to sit. Since then, the cup is waiting for me when I arrive, and I have come to see it less as a memorial than as an invitation she chose to keep open.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Dolores's habit by the end of the text?
options: Uneasy pity for a widow who cannot accept her husband's death
Mild amusement at a ritual she considers old-fashioned and odd
Polite indifference toward a routine that does not concern her
Grateful understanding of a gesture she now sees as welcoming
items.explanation: Daphne는 처음에 두 번째 잔을 조금 슬프고 이상하게 여겨 조심스럽게 피해 다녔다. 그러나 Dolores가 그 잔을 건네며 '그이도 쓰이길 바랄 것'이라고 말한 뒤, 화자는 그 잔을 추모가 아닌 열린 초대로 보게 된다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 처음의 인상에 가깝고 결말의 태도가 아니며, B의 재미와 C의 무관심은 화자의 변화된 감정과 맞지 않는다.
